issues.description: The prose in the problem statement (Part 2) requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) that takes a double parameter and includes the milk volume in its return string, but the UML, the example usage in the template Main, and the solution implementation define/messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This creates a signature mismatch: students following the prose would implement a different method signature than the interfaces and example code expect, causing compile errors or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent with the UML and template: change the prose in Part 2 to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and update the example return format to omit the volume (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Alternatively, if the intent was to include a milkVolume parameter, update the UML, the Milkable interface, the template Main usage, and the solution implementations to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and propagate the parameter to all calls and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the Milkable.messageOnMilk method: the UML and other parts of the statement (messageOnMilk():String) and the template/solution use a no-argument method, but a section in Part 2 instructs students to implement messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). This mismatch between a parameterless signature and a signature with a double parameter for the same conceptual method will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the Part 2 textual instruction to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and the return format "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (aligning with the UML, template Main usage, and solution), or (B) update the UML, template Main calls, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust all implementations and calls to pass and print the volume (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)"). Prefer option A to match the existing template and solution structure.
